gap: No result ChatGPT got states which replacement recorder lists the older standard-definition coax formats by name (Viewtron VT-DVR-8: CVBS at CIF, D1 and 960H), controls PTZ cameras over the coax (UTC), and records 4K/8MP coax cameras at only 7 fps (IP cameras get 30 fps). Dahua's cited XVR7208A-4K-I3 page says it auto-detects CVBS but gives no CVBS resolution.
standout_why: I compared the cited Dahua XVR7208A-4K-I3 product page (dahuasecurity.com) with the cited Hikvision DS-7208HQHI-S1/XT page, which redirected to hikvision.com and came back empty. I also checked the rest of the result set, which is all Dahua and Hikvision datasheets and product pages. The Dahua page already lists resolution and frame rate for CVI, TVI and AHD. It shows 4K TVI and 4K AHD capped at 15 fps, and it says AI features turn off once IP extension is enabled. So those facts are not new, and the AI limits were already in the cited result. None of the results name a non-Dahua/Hikvision recorder's CVBS resolutions, UTC PTZ over coax, or coax-vs-IP frame-rate split. ChatGPT's answer only mentions vague 'U.S. regulatory restrictions'. None of its results quotes FCC text naming Hikvision and Dahua as Covered List entities.
decides: This backs the Viewtron VT-DVR-8 as the pick when the existing cameras are older CVBS models or coax PTZ domes. It is the only candidate where a page I opened names 960H/D1/CIF CVBS support, states UTC PTZ, and states NDAA compliance. It also adds a warning: owners of 4K/8MP coax cameras get 7 fps on its BNC inputs. If those owners have TVI or AHD cameras, Dahua's 15 fps at 4K is better. For U.S. shoppers, the FCC Covered List status weighs against the two Dahua/Hikvision picks ChatGPT showed.

findings.label: Analog CCTV (CVBS) resolutions supported

findings.label: HD coax formats and resolutions
findings.value: AHD, HD-TVI, HD-CVI: 720p, 1080p, 3 MP, 4 MP, 5 MP, 8 MP/4K (same list for each format)
findings.source_title: Viewtron VT-DVR-8 8 channel DVR - CCTV Camera Pros
findings.note: The page lists one resolution set per format. It does not say whether each channel auto-detects the format.

findings.label: Recording frame rate per BNC camera
findings.value: 30 fps at 960H/720p/1080p; 15 fps at 4 MP; 12 fps at 5 MP; 7 fps at 4K/8 MP. IP cameras: 30 fps up to 4K/8 MP
findings.source_title: Viewtron VT-DVR-8 8 channel DVR - CCTV Camera Pros
findings.note: The same page also says '8fps@4K' in its summary block. I took 7 fps from the detailed spec list and flag the conflict.

findings.label: PTZ control over coax
findings.value: UTC (Up the Coax) PTZ control over RG59
findings.source_title: Viewtron VT-DVR-8 8 channel DVR - CCTV Camera Pros
findings.note: Quote: 'UTC (Up the Coax) Support to Control PTZ Over RG59 Video Cable'. The page also says RG59 or RG6 coax works.

findings.label: Inputs and storage
findings.value: 8 BNC + 8 IP (16 ch total); 2 drive bays, 12 TB each (24 TB total)
findings.source_title: Viewtron VT-DVR-8 8 channel DVR - CCTV Camera Pros
findings.note: The page conflicts on the included drive. The spec list says '1TB Hard Drive Included', and the summary says the unit includes a 2 TB drive. Our current page says 2 TB, so recheck before publishing.

findings.label: Stated exclusions
findings.value: Hard-wired only (no wireless cameras); no built-in AI/face recognition; the FAQ answers 'No' to built-in human detection
findings.source_title: Viewtron VT-DVR-8 8 channel DVR - CCTV Camera Pros
findings.note: The page's smart-motion section also says it can tell people from vehicles, which conflicts with the FAQ. Our 'Alerts and notes' cell should not claim human detection.

findings.label: Price
findings.source_title: Viewtron VT-DVR-8 8 channel DVR - CCTV Camera Pros
findings.note: The page also states 'NDAA compliant for government use' and a 2-year warranty.

findings.label: Coax formats and resolution per format
findings.value: CVI up to 4K at 25/30 fps; TVI 4K at 15 fps, 5 MP at 20 fps; AHD 4K at 15 fps, 5 MP at 20 fps; CVBS auto-detected but no resolution listed
findings.source_title: XVR7208A-4K-I3 8-Channel Penta-brid 4K WizSense DVR - Zhejiang Dahua Technology Co., Ltd.
findings.note: This page was a cited ChatGPT result, so this finding is not new. With Encode Enhancement on, only channels 1 and 5 record 4K at up to 30 fps, and the others are capped at 15 fps.

findings.label: Feature exclusions the maker states
findings.value: With IP extension enabled, EPTZ, Video Quality Analytics, Scene Changing, Face Recognition, Face Detection, SMD, Perimeter Protection, QuickPick 2.0 and Privacy Protection cannot be used. Face Recognition works on 2 channels only. Each drive holds up to 16 TB (2 bays)
findings.source_title: XVR7208A-4K-I3 8-Channel Penta-brid 4K WizSense DVR - Zhejiang Dahua Technology Co., Ltd.
findings.note: IP access: 8 IP channels by default, or up to 16 when analog channels are converted to IP. Audio over coax on all 8 BNC inputs.

findings.label: U.S. regulatory status of Hikvision and Dahua recorders
findings.value: Hikvision (Hangzhou Hikvision Digital Technology) and Dahua Technology, with affiliates and subsidiaries, are FCC Covered List entities. Under FCC 25-71 (released 2025-10-29, effective 2025-12-26), the FCC can bar future importation and marketing of previously authorized covered equipment without revoking the authorization
findings.source_title: FCC Small Entity Compliance Guide DA 26-48 (2026-01-13), Second Report and Order FCC 25-71, ET Docket 21-232
findings.note: The guide does not tie the importation/marketing limit to Hikvision or Dahua by name. It also does not quote the use-based scope (public safety, government facilities, critical infrastructure) of their video-surveillance listing. State only what is quoted here.
